3 Internet Stocks on Our Watchlist

By breaking down physical barriers, consumer internet businesses are reshaping how people shop, connect, learn, and play. This influence cuts both ways though because they have high exposure to the ups and downs of consumer spending, and uncertainty surrounding this factor has capped the industry's returns - over the past six months, its 7.3% gain has lagged the S&P 500 by 7.9 percentage points.

Despite the lackluster result, a few diamonds in the rough can produce earnings growth no matter what, and we started StockStory to help you find them. On that note, here are three resilient internet stocks at the top of our wish list.

Match Group (MTCH)

Market Cap: $9.38 billion

Originally started as a dial-up service before widespread internet adoption, Match (NASDAQ:MTCH) was an early innovator in online dating and today has a portfolio of apps including Tinder, Hinge, Archer, and OkCupid.

Why Are We Fans of MTCH?

Marketing expenses show it saves money by shying from over-the-top promotions to win new users

Highly efficient business model is illustrated by its impressive 37% EBITDA margin, and its profits increased over the last few years as it scaled

Strong free cash flow margin of 29.4% enables it to reinvest or return capital consistently, and its rising cash conversion increases its margin of safety

At $40.87 per share, Match Group trades at 9.2x forward EV/EBITDA. Is now the right time to buy? Find out in our full research report, it's free.

Remitly (RELY)

Market Cap: $4.85 billion

With Amazon founder Jeff Bezos as an early investor, Remitly (NASDAQ:RELY) is an online platform that enables consumers to safely and quickly send money globally.

Why Do We Love RELY?

Active Customers are rising, meaning the company can increase revenue without incurring additional customer acquisition costs if it can cross-sell additional products and features

Incremental sales over the last three years have been highly profitable as its earnings per share increased by 163% annually, topping its revenue gains

Free cash flow margin grew by 43.1 percentage points over the last few years, giving the company more chips to play with

Remitly's stock price of $23.04 implies a valuation ratio of 9.9x forward EV/EBITDA. Is now the time to initiate a position? See for yourself in our comprehensive research report, it's free.

Reddit (RDDT)

Market Cap: $29.38 billion

Founded in 2005 by two University of Virginia roommates, Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) facilitates user-generated content across niche communities (called subreddits) that discuss anything from stocks to dating and memes.

title: My Husband, 57, Swears The Market Will Crash And Wants $200,000 From His 401(k) To Buy A Solar Battery And Pay Debt — Even With $70K Penalty
detail:
My Husband, 57, Swears The Market Will Crash And Wants $200,000 From His 401(k) To Buy A Solar Battery And Pay Debt — Even With $70K Penalty
An older blonde woman with a confused expression talks on a phone, wearing a beige sweater. (Credit: Photo: fizkes/shutterstock)
Jeannine Mancini

RDDT

Sometimes the internet convinces people to buy a solar battery. Other times, it convinces them the financial apocalypse is coming and their retirement account needs to be emptied before Tuesday.

One Reddit user found herself dealing with the second scenario after her 57-year-old husband decided to withdraw $200,000 from his 401(k), leaving just $50,000 behind. She turned to Reddit because she wasn't sure how to explain why she thought the plan was a terrible idea.

The Next AI Winner Might Not Be A Chip Company. It Could Be The Companies Powering The Data Centers.

A $200,000 Withdrawal Came With A $70,000 Problem

The woman said her husband had been watching "prepping videos" warning that an economic collapse was near. His solution was to pull $200,000 from the retirement account and use the money to pay off their credit, buy an expensive solar battery and pay down their house.

The plan would leave the couple with about $50,000 in the 401(k), while taxes and penalties on the withdrawal would cost roughly $70,000, according to the post.

The husband wasn't concerned about those costs. He believed getting out of the market and becoming debt-free would protect the couple from the financial fallout he expected.

His wife wasn't convinced.

"I think this is a bad idea because common knowledge is to not touch the 401k," she wrote, adding that the taxes, penalties and fees were "huge."

She also said her husband didn't want to speak with a financial planner because he didn't trust them.

That left her asking Reddit for help finding the right words.

Trending: A Real Estate Investment With No House, No Tenant And No 10-Year Hold?

Reddit Wasn't Exactly Team 401(k) Withdrawal

The responses came down pretty firmly on one side.

One commenter warned that the couple was already behind on retirement savings and wrote, "If he does this he's going to work until he dies."

Another put it even more simply: "Even if the market crashed, it will recover. Leave the money alone."

Then came the less diplomatic assessment. "Your husband is a buffoon."

Another commenter argued that taking the money out could create a financial disaster of its own, writing, "If you touch that 401k prematurely you're going to have your own version of a collapse and financial ruin."

One Redditor argued that the couple was already behind on retirement savings. The numbers tell a more nuanced story. With roughly $250,000 in the 401(k), the 57-year-old husband was sitting around the published median for people in their 50s, according to Empower data. That doesn't mean the couple was fully prepared for retirement, but it also doesn't suggest they were hopelessly behind.

title: Reddit Plunges 36% Year to Date: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?

Reddit Plunges 36% Year to Date: Should You Buy the Stock on the Dip?
Nilanshi Mukherjee
Mon, October 5, 2026 at 8:59 AM MDT 5 min read
RDDT
PINS
META
SNAP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Reddit RDDT shares have plunged 35.7% in the year-to-date period, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer & Technology sector's 24.7% increase. The Zacks Internet - Software industry has also increased 10% in the same time frame.

The company's shares have also underperformed its peers, which include Pinterest PINS, Meta Platforms META and Snap SNAP. These companies are expanding their footprint in the digital advertising market. Shares of Meta Platforms have gained 10.3%, while Pinterest and Snap have lost 25.6% and 30.9%, respectively, in the year-to-date period.

The dip can be explained by irregular and declining search referral traffic, especially toward the end of the second quarter of 2026, causing a slight decrease in the number of daily active users and increasing volatility. The lack of insight into external search trends still poses a problem. Difficult macroeconomic uncertainties and the intense competition in the digital advertising market remain concerns.

RDDT Stock Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Despite these headwinds, Reddit's expanding advertising portfolio, strong user engagement, including rising daily and weekly active users, gains in Average Revenue Per Unique (ARPU) and the expansion of advertiser tools such as Dynamic Product Ads, Reddit Pixel and CAPI have been key catalysts. These factors are helping Reddit to fend off its competitors like Pinterest, Snap and Meta Platforms.

RDDT Benefits From Expanding Portfolio

Reddit's expanding portfolio has been a key catalyst in driving the company's user engagement. In the second quarter of 2026, Reddit reported 130.3 million daily active uniques, up 18% year over year, and 514.6 million weekly active uniques, up 24% year over year.

RDDT is benefiting from successful product innovation and user engagement strategies. The company's focus on improving the experience for new users, particularly through updated feed models and easier posting mechanisms, has led to a 50% year-over-year increase in new app user retention in the second quarter of 2026. Features like video in comments and interactive games have expanded engagement opportunities. At the same time, efforts to convert web users to app users have resulted in higher retention and more valuable user cohorts.

The company's innovation in its ad stack has been a major growth driver. The launch and rapid adoption of Reddit Max, an AI-driven suite for ad automation and optimization, has delivered significant results. Advertiser usage of Max grew more than 60% from the first quarter, and revenues from Max campaigns increased by more than 150%. Features like tailored creatives and dynamic product ads are helping brands achieve better outcomes, such as Lenovo's 40% higher purchase value with Max campaigns compared to standard campaigns.

Further expanding its portfolio, in September 2026, Reddit made its AI-powered Max campaigns available to all advertisers following a beta launch earlier this year. Max campaigns automate targeting, creative selection, placements, and budget allocation while allowing advertisers to retain strategic control. Reddit said early tests delivered 17% lower cost per acquisition and more than 27% higher conversions versus standard campaigns. The company also added Advertising API support, integration with Smartly and new asset groups, enabling advertisers to manage multiple creative sets within a single campaign and assess performance separately.

Investors are paying closer attention to businesses that rely on their own cash generation and solid balance sheets instead of cheap credit. This article looks at three financially robust U.S. stocks with high return on equity and historically strong fundamentals that may appeal to investors seeking quality first.

The stocks covered next are just a sample set, and the broader screen surfaced 23 more companies with similarly compelling balance sheets, cash generation and return on equity profiles that are not listed in this article.

If you want to identify, filter and analyze those extra candidates alongside the ones discussed here, head straight to the Solid Balance Sheet and Fundamentals screener.

Reddit (RDDT)

Reddit is the first stock from the Solid Balance Sheet and Fundamentals screener because its ad driven community platform converts deep user engagement into high return on equity and strong cash generation that directly support a resilient financial position.

Reddit operates a global digital forum where users share posts, videos and comments across interest based communities, generating US$2.78b in revenue mainly from advertising, with roughly US$2.23b from the United States, and the stock valued at about US$28.77b today.

Reddit Inc. (RDDT) closed at $147.86 in the latest trading session, marking a -1.12% move from the prior day. This change lagged the S&P 500's 0.73% gain on the day. Elsewhere, the Dow saw an upswing of 0.49%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq appreciated by 1.19%.

The company's shares have seen a decrease of 4.14% over the last month, not keeping up with the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 6.36% and the S&P 500's gain of 0.55%.

Investors will be eagerly watching for the performance of Reddit Inc. in its upcoming earnings disclosure. It is anticipated that the company will report an EPS of $1.3, marking a 62.5% rise compared to the same quarter of the previous year. Meanwhile, our latest consensus estimate is calling for revenue of $886.35 million, up 51.54% from the prior-year quarter.

Looking at the full year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates suggest analysts are expecting earnings of $5.27 per share and revenue of $3.4 billion. These totals would mark changes of +101.15% and +54.16%, respectively, from last year.

Any recent changes to analyst estimates for Reddit Inc. should also be noted by investors. These revisions typically reflect the latest short-term business trends, which can change frequently. Hence, positive alterations in estimates signify analyst optimism regarding the business and profitability.

Our research shows that these estimate changes are directly correlated with near-term stock prices. Investors can capitalize on this by using the Zacks Rank. This model considers these estimate changes and provides a simple, actionable rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, stretching from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), has a noteworthy track record of outperforming, validated by third-party audits, with stocks rated #1 producing an average annual return of +25% since the year 1988. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate has witnessed an unchanged state. Reddit Inc. is holding a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy) right now.

In terms of valuation, Reddit Inc. is presently being traded at a Forward P/E ratio of 28.36. This denotes a premium relative to the industry average Forward P/E of 19.59.

It's also important to note that RDDT currently trades at a PEG ratio of 0.69. The PEG ratio is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but this metric also takes the company's expected earnings growth rate into account. The Internet - Software industry had an average PEG ratio of 1.17 as trading concluded yesterday.

The Internet - Software industry is part of the Computer and Technology sector. At present, this industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank of 92, placing it within the top 38% of over 250 industries.
